evaluation_units.flagship_showcase: One purposively selected, transparently iterated human-Agent case is the descriptive unit. It is not sampled from a defined population and supplies no success-rate denominator.
evaluation_units.candidate_version: Every candidate and revision remains in the append-only discovery trace but is not an independent replicate of system performance.
evaluation_units.artifact: Artifacts and claims are nested evidence and never inflate a denominator.

showcase_terminal_disposition.landed_reportable: The locked flagship passes deterministic feasibility, executes the approved analysis once, produces all mandatory artifacts, and passes evidence-bound scientific review without postresult repair.
showcase_terminal_disposition.landed_restricted: The locked flagship executes, but diagnostics or evidence impose a prespecified restriction that is transparently carried into the report.
showcase_terminal_disposition.safe_nonlanding: The locked flagship terminates at a legitimate identification, data-authority, feasibility, or publication gate without postoutcome substitution of another idea.
showcase_terminal_disposition.workflow_failure: The workflow fails for an agent-caused, artifact, budget, execution, or contract reason that is not a scientifically appropriate gate.

mandatory_showcase_artifacts: sealed authentic broad research direction and iterative discovery contract
complete versioned query and retrieval ledger
clinical and methods feedback, rejection reasons, and decision log
final selected-idea, protocol-lock, and phase-B declaration receipts
code, cohort, result, diagnostic, and sensitivity artifacts when execution is authorized
bounded report, limitations, and manuscript-ready paragraph
tokens, cost, wall time, Provider and retrieval calls, failed executions, iteration rounds, and human minutes

iterative_candidate_review.timing: Discovery feedback and final selection occur before patient-level outcome analysis. Deterministic feasibility summaries may inform preoutcome iteration, but patient rows and outcome results are hidden from phase-A Provider calls and human candidate selection.
iterative_candidate_review.iteration_rule: Reviewers may request multiple generate-critique-revise rounds within the frozen phase-A budget. Every score, comment, revision, rejection, feasibility failure, and decision is appended with a timestamp; earlier versions are never overwritten.
iterative_candidate_review.final_lock_rule: The reviewers approve one flagship and its analysis plan after deterministic feasibility but before patient-level outcome analysis. After the phase-B declaration, no outcome-driven question, endpoint, database, method, or candidate switch may replace it.
iterative_candidate_review.reliability: Report the two reviewers' scores, disagreements, and resolution descriptively. The showcase does not estimate reviewer reliability or system-level success.

showcase_domains.pass_rule: The initial direction, evidence maps, all candidate versions, feedback, revisions, rejections, feasibility checks, final selection, and protocol lock are complete and temporally ordered.
The locked question specifies population, exposure or index, outcome, time origin, estimand, method, missing-data policy, diagnostics, sensitivities, and claim ceiling before outcome analysis.
Every required concept and identity boundary has a passing source-authority and deterministic feasibility receipt before phase B.
The locked plan is executed once with complete code, denominators, results, diagnostics, sensitivities, and terminal receipt, or terminates at a documented safe gate.
Every headline number and manuscript claim resolves to a retained artifact and digest, with no unbound or manually inserted result.
The report discloses purposive selection and human contribution and reflects null or positive results, limitations, scope reductions, and failed diagnostics without upgrading authority.

prespecified_descriptive_outputs: candidate funnel by iteration round: generated, revised, rejected, feasibility-checked, selected, executed, and landed
all reviewer feedback, candidate revisions, rejection reasons, and unresolved reservations
mandatory-artifact completeness and showcase-domain pass or fail
time, tokens, billed cost, Provider and retrieval calls, failed executions, iteration rounds, and human minutes by phase
all safe gates, restrictions, workflow failures, and preoutcome feasibility failures
one evidence-lineage diagram and one receipt-linked end-to-end product timeline

analysis_rules.uncertainty: No case-sampling interval is calculated because the flagship is purposively selected and no population sampling frame exists.
analysis_rules.missing_artifact: A missing mandatory artifact fails the relevant showcase domain and remains visible; it is not repaired after the terminal timestamp.

claim_ceiling: The rubric supports a transparent flagship demonstration of iterative human-Agent idea development, governed execution, and evidence landing. It does not support claims of superior ideation, universal novelty, autonomous discovery, a landing probability, representative performance, increased publication output, or improved clinical outcomes.
